intent: To illustrate that before the 2020 election, voters had higher confidence in in-person voting than in mail-in voting, supporting the narration's point about unfamiliarity with mail-in methods.

requirements.question: Is the in-person vs. mail-in Very-confidence comparison obligatory from the intent?

units.claim: In-person polling places has a higher relative 'Very' confidence value than absentee/mail-in ballot (0.2680 vs. 0.1094).
accept: In-person Very confidence is higher than mail-in Very confidence.
The in-person polling-place mark for Very exceeds the absentee/mail-in mark for Very.
Voters are more likely to be Very confident in in-person voting than in mail-in voting.
units.evidence: The mark for In person at polling places under Very must extend farther than the mark for By absentee or mail-in ballot under Very.

optional_valid: The four relative values order as In-person Very > 49 Somewhat > 20 Somewhat > Mail-in Very.
The mail-in Very relative value is less than half of the in-person Very relative value.
The in-person Very relative value is smaller than the sum of the two Somewhat relative values.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
